summary: Phase B — Products console v3 backend testing. 12/13 tests passed (92%). All new Phase B endpoints (KPIs, sales-30d, bulk-status, bulk-promo, product history, brand PATCH rename cascade) work correctly. Phase A regression (search-suggestions, best-sellers, pos/shortcuts, waitlist) still passes. One real bug: POST /api/products silently drops the 14 new fields because the ProductIn Pydantic schema was not extended for Phase B.

critical.issue: ProductIn Pydantic model (server.py L66-70) does not declare the Phase B fields price_old, status, collections, tags, material, occasion, heel_type, care, supplier, alert_threshold, featured, is_new, seo_title, seo_description. Pydantic drops them via model_dump() before insert, so a creation request that includes them persists the product without any of these fields. PATCH works because update_product uses Dict[str,Any]. Fix: extend ProductIn with Optional fields, or switch create_product to accept Dict[str,Any] like update does.

action_items: Extend ProductIn in /app/backend/server.py (around L66) with the 14 new optional fields so POST /api/products persists them (same shape as PATCH already supports). Suggested additions: price_old: Optional[int]=None; status: str='actif'; collections: List[str]=[]; tags: List[str]=[]; material: Optional[str]=None; occasion: Optional[str]=None; heel_type: Optional[str]=None; care: Optional[str]=None; supplier: Optional[str]=None; alert_threshold: Optional[int]=None; featured: bool=False; is_new: bool=False; seo_title: Optional[str]=None; seo_description: Optional[str]=None.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py file is ~2810 lines — well beyond the 700-line guideline. Should be split into routers per domain (products, orders, pos, brands, cms, rider, etc.).
ProductIn drops unknown fields on POST while PATCH uses raw Dict; schema divergence between create and update is a frequent source of silent data loss. Keep both aligned.
bulk-promo endpoint has `raise HTTPException(400)` without a message — should include an explanatory detail (same as bulk-status).
update_brand uses upsert=True on PATCH /brands/{bid} — a bad id would silently create a half-empty brand doc. Prefer update_one without upsert and 404 if not found.
seed_data_creation: Test created and cleaned up one brand (TEST_BrandA→TEST_BrandB) and one product (TEST_PhaseB_Product). bulk-promo prices restored via PATCH after test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase B endpoints all pass. Only remaining fix is extending the ProductIn Pydantic schema. Reusable test file at /app/backend/tests/test_products_phase_b.py — re-run after the schema fix; the test_create_with_new_fields_returned should flip to green and 13/13 will pass.
rca of the issue: Pydantic v2 BaseModel ignores unknown fields by default; create_product calls body.model_dump() which filters input to the fields declared on ProductIn. Since Phase B added fields only in the frontend form & in PATCH handler, POST silently discards them. Reproduction: POST /api/products with any of the 14 new keys → GET /api/products returns the created product without those keys. Mitigation: add the fields to ProductIn (preferred) or change create_product signature to `body: Dict[str, Any]` and validate manually.
